name: [P1 · GAMEPLAY-DIALOGUE] Expand contextual dialogue and meaningful conversation options
description:
GAMEPLAY-DIALOGUE

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03.

Add richer suspect dialogue and distinct player approaches using the original Git-history mechanics. Preserve free text and voice; optional suggested approaches should depend on revealed evidence and never expose hidden solutions. Acceptance: playable branching examples; repetition/diversity checks; accessible controls; no fabricated clue progress; compare with baseline game.

name: [P1 · GAMEPLAY-TACTICS] Make red-team tactics interactive and consequential
description:
GAMEPLAY-TACTICS

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03.

Design and implement a small fictional-case tactical loop: probe assumptions, challenge claims, test contradictions and recover from failed tactics. Explain risk/reward, distinguish persuasive bluff from evidence and avoid arbitrary hidden penalties. Acceptance: seeded cases show different tactical outcomes, fair feedback and solvability; no real-target intrusion tooling.

name: [P1 · GAMEPLAY-EVIDENCE] Connect evidence, statements and contradiction challenges
description:
GAMEPLAY-EVIDENCE

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03.

Let players inspect known evidence, connect it to suspect statements and issue a focused challenge. Preserve noir presentation and existing accusation goal. Acceptance: evidence traceability, keyboard path, no future-secret leaks, validated contradiction progression and coherent reveals across replay/live providers.

name: [P1 · GAMEPLAY-EVAL] Red-team the game and test whether the new loop is fun and fair
description:
GAMEPLAY-EVAL

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03.

Use full Git-history intent plus gameplay research to build an evaluation set for direct/indirect probes, false premises, repeated questions, off-topic pressure, prompt injection, malformed AI responses and alternate valid accusations. Acceptance: measured outcomes, fair judgments, diverse dialogue, difficulty/accessibility comparison and real playtest/rehearsal evidence. Do not equate automated scores with proven fun.

name: [P1 · DOCS] Update all project documentation to the implemented product
description:
DOCS

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03.

Refresh README, setup, env examples, architecture, module ownership, providers, local Codex vs hosted API, voice, migrations, test commands, troubleshooting, privacy/data retention and demo rehearsal. Preserve historical audit as baseline. Acceptance: commands executed on fresh setup; every claim/config reference matches code and proof; no credentials committed. Update incrementally, final review after implementation.

name: [P2 · SITE] Build the project website after the game acceptance pass
description:
SITE

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03.

Create a polished public-facing project website consistent with the completed noir game. Explain gameplay and the red-team concept, show final media, supported demo access and verified capabilities. Dependency: game acceptance complete. Acceptance: responsive/keyboard/contrast/performance checks; links/media work; clear live/demo/replay status. Build locally before publishing; confirm actual hosting target at that stage.

name: [P2 · PORTFOLIO] Build and add the jason.theft.studio case study
description:
PORTFOLIO

User-authorized scope addition, 2026-10-03. Correct portfolio: https://jason.theft.studio

After the game is verified, inspect jason.theft.studio and its source to match existing case-study structure, typography, navigation and visual style. Tell the evidence-backed hackathon-to-upgrade story: role, problem, gameplay/design decisions, AI/voice architecture, constraints, before/after, actual results and reflection. Integrate into portfolio with correct project links and media. Acceptance: design match and responsive/keyboard checks; all claims trace to evidence; user reviews final narrative; no invented metrics or achievements.

name: [P1 · GAMEPLAY-MAP] Show a simple conversation path after win or loss
desc:
User scope addition, 3 Oct 2026.

Add a compact conversation flowchart to both outcome screens, matching the existing noir/case-file style. Show the path actually taken and which evidence challenges/accusations were supported or wrong. Keep ordinary questions neutral unless authoritative evidence supports a judgment; do not invent alternative branches or label dialogue from stress/tone.

Acceptance: win and loss both show a readable responsive path; exact source text is inspectable; wrong-then-right accusations retain their own verdict; evidence links connect the challenged statement and exhibit; keyboard and reduced-motion support; no color-only meaning. Long conversations remain manageable. Verify result reload/recovery and truthful canonical outcome data, then inspect in the browser when authorized.

Implementation checkpoint · 3 Oct 2026
Win/loss path implemented with canonical evidence and accusation verdicts, source details and explicit unverified live wording. Real localhost Codex win and give-up loss both executed; result reload retains the path. Evidence: docs/audit/evidence/local-http-gameplay-map.json and result-conversation-path tests. Browser layout/keyboard/reduced-motion inspection pending.
